judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default rate is fixed at four points over the rate "otherwise applicable to Base Rate Loans," yet it applies to all Obligations including LIBOR Rate Loans, so the base of the calculation is not the rate those loans actually bear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(a) converts LIBOR Loans to Base Rate on default, which largely reconciles the mismatch; Section 2.5(e) caps the result at the lawful maximum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear monthly-in-arrears payment rule with an authorization to charge amounts to the Loan Account; the compounding sentence is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening carve-out ("Except as provided to the contrary in Section 2.10") ties to the fee provisions, and Section 2.9 records the charges, all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 360-day/actual-days convention stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Section 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause, which is the standard pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional usury savings clause; the "ipso facto" retroactivity language is unusual but its effect is spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.10(e)'s minimum interest charge carries its own non-usurious proviso, so the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section requires Collections to be deposited "into a bank account in Fund's name" even though both Fund and Manager are Borrowers, separately requires sale and payoff proceeds to be routed to a Cash Management Account (implying such proceeds may not be "Collections"), and then declares that after 60 days Wells Fargo "shall be the only Cash Management Bank." Those three commands do not sit comfortably together in one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 2.6 designates Greater Bay Bank and Mechanics Bank, Schedule 5.18 shows the operating accounts, Section 2.6(c) contemplates adding banks, and Section 6.12(d) forbids other depository accounts — so who may hold which cash, and where sale proceeds must go, has to be resolved across those provisions and the Permitted Dispositions definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prescribes three required terms of each Cash Management Agreement in definite language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The daily-sweep requirement to Lender's Account fits Sections 2.7 and 2.9, though it must be squared with Section 2.6(e)'s permission for Borrowers to draw on Escrow Accounts daily.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Amendment mechanics with two different cure windows (30 and 60 days) keyed to different Lender judgments; detailed but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes multiple Cash Management Banks whereas Section 2.6(a) says Wells Fargo will be the only one after 60 days, a tension between adjacent subsections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short grant of a Lien in the accounts; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces Borrower Collateral clause (d) and Section 4.1; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph defines "Escrow Account" and then imposes obligations on "such Cash Management Account," mixing the two defined terms, and the carve-out for "accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower" is undefined in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 6.17's requirement that all escrowed amounts go into a Lender-perfected Deposit Account, Section 6.12(d)'s account prohibition and Section 2.6(b)'s daily sweep, which the daily withdrawal right cuts against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise rules on when a payment item counts as received; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the 1:00 p.m. cut-off in Section 2.3(a) and the Loan Account crediting in Section 2.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence contains a duplicated verb ("agrees to establish establish") and authorizes Lender to advance on instructions "from anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person," a strikingly loose authorization.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That authorization is looser than the Section 2.2(a) borrowing procedure and its cross-reference to Section 2.5(c) for advances "without instructions" is oblique.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional account-stated clause with a 30-day objection window and a manifest-error exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5(c) and 2.7; Bank Product Obligations are excluded from the Loan Account, matching Section 2.5(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed sum, fully earned on a stated date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the non-refundability lead-in of Section 2.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause reads "a monthly loan administration equal to $2,000" — the noun "fee" is missing, though the heading supplies it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere contradicts a $2,000 monthly administration fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee is stated as "one-half of one percent (0.30%)" — the words say 0.50% and the numeral says 0.30%, a self-contradiction on the face of the pricing term. That is a textbook mechanical error that changes what is owed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision resolves which figure governs; Section 2.10's lead-in only makes fees non-refundable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Per-diem and actual-cost fee provisions, definite in amount and trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the Lender Expenses definition clauses (c) and (g), which cap by reference to "any limitation contained in this Agreement."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense make-whole computation payable "on the first day of each calendar quarter and on the Maturity Date" during a period that ends eleven months after closing, so the final stub quarter's calculation is not clearly specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Unused Line Fee in Section 2.10(c), which uses the same $20,000,000 floor during the same period, raising a double-charging question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard capital-adequacy yield protection clause, but the payment window is rendered "within $0 days," an obvious corruption of the deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere fixes the period; the amounts become Lender Expenses/Obligations in the ordinary way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the LIBOR option and automatic conversion at period end; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (c) then deems the LIBOR Option elected absent contrary notice, which is the reverse of the default this subsection implies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise notice deadlines with a telephonic alternative and same-day written confirmation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit L-1's form contemplates notice "not less than 3 Business Days" before the month, matching this subsection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule is clearly expressed, but it reverses the default assumed by Section 2.12(a) and by Section 2.5(a)(ii), so which rate applies absent any notice is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.5(a) treats Base Rate as the residual rate while this subsection makes LIBOR the residual, a genuine internal inconsistency in the interest mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Market-disruption clause keyed to Lender's "reasonable opinion" that funding is "unlawful or impractical"; "impractical" is soft but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the LIBOR Rate definition and Section 2.12(a)'s conversion mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence disclaimer of matched funding; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Base LIBOR Rate definition's reference to quotation sources.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital of consideration for joint and several liability; declaratory rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports Sections 2.13(b)-(d) and 16.11; the mutual-benefit recital could be tested against the reality that only Fund holds the collateral, but the operative text is clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear co-debtor formulation, marred only by a typographical cross-reference to "Section 2.133."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Obligations definition and the Borrowers' joint treatment in the Loan Account under Section 16.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence imposing cross-payment duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.13(b) and (d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It declares the obligations absolute "irrespective of the validity, regularity or enforceability of this Agreement," a sweeping formulation, and it cross-refers to "Section 2.15," which does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is plainly Section 2.13, but the error appears in the very subsection making liability unconditional, and it sits against Section 16.4's severability regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of waived notices and defenses closing with "all demands, notices and other formalities of every kind"; a general catch-all after specifics, though qualified by "except as otherwise provided in this Agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exception has to be reconciled with the many notice rights the Agreement does give Borrowers (Sections 9.1(k), 12), which is a workable reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Representations and covenants about staying informed; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the suretyship waivers in the surrounding subsections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific waiver of election-of-remedies defenses, expressly referencing California Code of Civil Procedure section 580(d); the reference is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(a) makes New York law govern, so a California statutory waiver imported into a New York-law contract creates a real question about what it accomplishes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subparagraph (ii)(B) says "Agent and Lenders may collect from such Borrower" although this bilateral agreement has no Agent and a single Lender — leftover syndicated-form language in an operative waiver.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined parties are "Lender" and "Borrowers" (preamble, Section 14.1), so these undefined actors have no referent, and the California anti-deficiency waivers again sit against the New York choice of law in Section 13(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States who may enforce the section and that it revives on avoided payments; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 16.7's revival provision, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deferral of contribution and subrogation until payment in full in cash; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.13(k) and the "paid in full" definition in Section 2.3(b)(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turnover-trustee language triggered by a Default or Event of Default; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Directs collections to Section 2.3(b)'s waterfall, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete deliverable condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Filing Authorization Letter definition and Section 4.4(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of six closing documents, each a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Each listed document is defined and included in Loan Documents; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard secretary's-certificate condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Uses "Board of Directors" and "Authorized Person," both defined to fit LLCs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple document-delivery condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Governing Documents definition and Section 7.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a good standing certificate "dated within 36 days of the Closing Date," an odd figure alongside the 30-day requirement in the very next subsection, suggesting a transcription error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(f) uses 30 days for the same kind of certificate, an inconsistency between adjacent conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Foreign-qualification certificates keyed to whether failure would be a Material Adverse Change; definite apart from that soft standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.8(a)'s qualification representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Insurance certificate condition tied to Section 6.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8's requirements are the referenced standard; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Opinion-of-counsel condition in satisfactory form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere qualifies it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tax-compliance evidence condition with a Permitted Protest exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the covenant in Section 6.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad due-diligence condition whose satisfaction is entirely in Lender's judgment, listing several specific reviews; the closing phrase "the results of which shall be satisfactory to Lender" is unbounded but this is a closing condition only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It references Borrowers' underwriting guidelines, tying to Borrower's Required Procedures and Section 3.1(m); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reference checks "satisfactory to Lender in its sole discretion" — an absolute discretion standard, but as a condition precedent it is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agreement elsewhere uses Permitted Discretion and reasonableness standards; this one is deliberately harsher.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall have paid or shall pay with the initial Advance" is a slightly odd formulation for a condition precedent but its meaning is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Lender Expenses definition and Section 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires Lender's receipt and approval of the Required Procedures and form loan documents; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Borrower's Required Procedures definition (approval before the Closing Date) and Section 7.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard numerical closing test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 7.16(a)'s $600,000,000 ongoing covenant exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific address for a landlord waiver; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That address matches Schedules 5.5 and 5.7(b), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires counsel to be satisfied that the loan forms give "appropriate rights and remedies"; a soft standard, but again only a closing condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with Section 3.1(m) and Section 5.3's compliance representation without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition demands all licenses and full securities-law compliance, then provides that it "may be satisfied by Fund providing to Lender such reasonable assurances as Lender may require" — a proviso that substantially undoes the condition it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 makes the same compliance an absolute representation, so the softening proviso here sits against an unqualified warranty there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A review condition listing four specific portfolio items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the collateral reporting regime in Section 6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Financial statement review condition with specific dates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.3's ongoing reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed eight-item document checklist tied to a $250,000,000 threshold; the qualifiers "if available" on the appraisal and settlement statement soften two items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same $250,000,000 package recurs in Sections 3.3(e), 4.2 and 8.17, and Section 6.18 mis-cites it as "Section 3.3(z)," so the cross-referencing is imperfect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all — "all other documents and legal matters ... shall be in form and substance satisfactory to Lender" — appended to twenty specific conditions, which is the classic general-after-specific construction problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 3.1's lead-in (the making of the initial extension of credit is conclusive evidence of satisfaction or waiver), the catch-all is spent at closing, which defuses much of the risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is numbered "4.2" in the text although it is the Conditions Subsequent section, and it contains the grammatical slip "shall have a hired a full time Controller." Its single condition is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(c) makes failure of "a condition subsequent set forth in Section 3.2" an Event of Default, so the mis-numbering breaks the cross-reference chain that gives this provision teeth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bring-down of representations "in all material respects," with an earlier-date carve-out; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the lead-in to Section 5 and the Compliance Certificate's paragraphs 2 and 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: No-Default condition; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Default and Event of Default definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: No-injunction condition; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.6's related Event of Default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line condition resting entirely on the vague defined term "Material Adverse Change," including its "prospects" limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the standard used in Sections 3.1(f), 6.10, 8.9 and 8.13; the vagueness lies in the definition rather than in any conflict.
